Resolves #21393

The neo themes' default button is now compact: 32 px tall, 12 px padding and 0.875rem text, where it was the Portal's 48 px call to action. A toolbar's buttons take the toolbar size of the nearest theme: `:where(.neo-toolbar)` reads `--toolbar-button-*`, which every theme declares on its own scope. A toolbar therefore stays compact under an ancestor that raises the size, and a classic scope nested inside a neo one keeps its classic toolbar buttons. A container's own size still wins: the desktop taskbar keeps 40 px. The Portal's viewport and header opt back into the design system's large size, and every Portal button measures as on `dev`. No example changes: they all inherit the compact size, the ones still to come included.

Evidence: L3 (live Chromium frames of `dev` and of this head, plus a button inventory of all 24 neo-themed examples and apps before and after) → L3 required (AC-2 to AC-4 are visual reads; AC-5 runs in CI). Residual: none.

Change class: restoration (`fix`). agent-preflight: not hosted here; the pre-commit and pre-push guards ran.

A classic toolbar nested under a neo root matches a classic button in its scope. Outside-CI: the inventory below. No toolbar button outside the Portal header is above 32 px except the ones that size themselves: the taskbar's 40 px, tab strips, column headers |

      **Details:** You were right. A descendant selector cannot express "the nearest theme wins", but inheritance can.
      - **The new reset:** `src/toolbar/Base.css` gains `:where(.neo-toolbar)`, which reads `--toolbar-button-*`. Every theme declares those tokens on its own scope: the neo themes the compact 32 px, the classic themes their default button. So in a nested scope the nearest theme wins, at zero specificity: the taskbar's 40 px and the Portal header still win.
      - **The neo button files** now keep the compact default on the theme scope only.
      - **Why the tokens state values:** they do not reference `--button-*`. A toolbar that carries its own theme class would otherwise form a custom-property cycle in the neo themes, where both rules are zero-specificity.
      - **Your control:** `test/playwright/component/toolbar/ButtonSize.spec.mjs` is page-realm DOM over the built sheets, run under both neo themes.
